name: influenza-crossparadigm
title: Influenza cross-paradigm — one Sego 2022 blueprint, two mechanical substrates
description:
This investigation is the capstone of the `viva-multicell-blueprint` build: it
ties together the backend-neutral blueprint (Task 17), the `compile(blueprint,
backend)` compiler (Task 13), both real backends running the full model (fields
Task 6, rules Task 7, systemic ODE fed live by CellCountStep Task 21, immune
recruitment via latent-pool activation Task 20, real footprints Task 19), the
comparison layer (`viva_multicell_blueprint.compare` — identity, raster, metrics)
and the three interactive figures (`viva_multicell_blueprint.viz`).

**Blueprint update.** The recruitment design (Task 20) activates a PRE-PLACED
LATENT immune pool, so the Sego blueprint's `initial_state` now pre-places 12
size-25 latent immune cells (M/NK/CD8_latent) at the tissue margins via
`extra_blocks`; the `infected_seed` is scoped to the main epithelial block so the
latent pool never changes the infected count. All cells are size 25 (size-9 cells
dissolve). Parameters stay faithful to Sego 2022 params.yaml @ b952eec2.

**Runnable artifact.** `viva_multicell_blueprint.composites.sego.sego_crossparadigm`
(a `@composite_generator`, parameterized by `backend` and `blueprint`) is the
baseline composite for every study and drives the dashboard Composite Explorer.

**Reduced scale.** Every study runs at a TRACTABLE reduced scale (a 50x50-site
patch, a 6x6 epithelial block) so the runs actually complete; this is a
demonstration, not paper scale. The comparison is reproducible (fixed seeds).

**Anti-goal respected.** No parameter is tuned to force the two backends to
agree. Honest divergence is reported.

at_a_glance.role: §9.1. Mechanics-only sheet on both backends; sweep the neutral adhesion -> (CPM J, vertex tension). Comparable shape stats (mean area 23.6 CPM / 34.9 vertex, CV 0.10 / 0.06); the J<->tension mapping is DIRECTIONAL, not pinned (vertex CV spread < 0.01 across scale). tension_scale = 1.0 retained.

§9.2. Both backends reproduce the blueprint t=0 state. CPM exact (centroid RMS 0.000 um); vertex clean 1:1 (fraction_clean 1.0, 0 unmapped) with a sub-cell residual (RMS 1.21 um). 48/48 type match on both.

§9.3 CAPSTONE. Full Sego model on both backends; three comparison families + three figures, judged against a NULL CONTROL (same-backend seed-to-seed spread). Headline: on fate + patch LOCATION the cross-backend difference falls inside the same-backend seed spread (cross fate 0.942 vs CPM 0.934 / vertex 0.943; vertex 100% inside the CPM envelope) → we FAIL TO REJECT a substrate effect at this scale/seed count (null, not equality). The one exception: raw occupancy IoU trends ~25-35% below both baselines (0.165 vs 0.249/0.212) — a candidate weak signal to test at larger scale / more vertex seeds.

§9 stretch. Sweep initial viral load over seeds; both substrates agree on the STRICT DIRECTION — the highest dose ends with more infection than the lowest on every backend and seed (CPM 1->7/1->2, vertex 0->5/1->6). Directional, not a dose-response curve.

glossary.definition: Running the same model on two different mechanical substrates (CPM voxel vs vertex polygon) and comparing.
Pre-placed resting immune cells (M/NK/CD8_latent) at the tissue margin that recruitment activates in place (type switch), rather than inserting new topology.
Fraction of the t0 cohort in the same state (type, or alive-vs-dead) at each step across the two backends.
Intersection-over-union of the two backends' rasterized cell footprints (CPM voxel occupancy vs vertex face polygons).

question: Can ONE backend-neutral blueprint express the whole Sego 2022 influenza model (ViralInfectionVTM) and run it faithfully on two different mechanical substrates — a Cellular Potts model (viva-cpm) and a vertex model (vivarium-tyssue) — and where do the two substrates agree vs diverge when the shared mechanism is driven live?
hypothesis: Because the field / rules / systemic-ODE / latent-pool recruitment mechanism is compiled BYTE-FOR-BYTE identically onto both backends and only the single mechanics node differs, cell-FATE dynamics should be nearly backend-independent, while SPATIAL morphology should diverge — each substrate samples the shared field at its own cell centroid and measures cell-cell contact through its own geometry. Divergence is therefore expected and is a finding about the substrate, not a bug.

The full Sego blueprint runs on BOTH backends at reduced scale; per-cell agreement, dynamics-with-band, and spatial-pattern + occupancy IoU are all computed, the three figures render under the inline cap, and the agree/diverge result is reported honestly.
Both backends agree on the monotone direction of infection vs initial viral load.

executive.what_is_this: The capstone cross-paradigm demonstration: one backend-neutral Sego 2022 influenza blueprint, compiled and run on both a Cellular Potts and a vertex substrate, with a full three-family comparison and three interactive figures.
executive.verdict: The architecture holds. One blueprint runs the FULL Sego model (fields, rules, live systemic ODE, latent-pool recruitment) on both backends, and because the mechanism is shared byte-for-byte the mechanical substrate is the only possible source of cross-paradigm difference. Judged against a NULL CONTROL (same-backend seed-to-seed spread), on cell fate and infected-patch LOCATION the cross-backend difference falls inside the same-backend seed spread, so we FAIL TO REJECT a substrate effect at this scale and seed count (a null result, NOT proof of equality): cross-backend fate agreement 0.942 (N=400), within the same-backend baselines (CPM 0.934, vertex 0.943; equal 0.987 at CI scale); patch location 6.1 um cross vs 5.4 um same-backend; vertex trajectory inside the CPM 3-seed envelope at 100% of steps. Final cell areas match (24.7 vs 24.5), so the spatial comparison is not representation-confounded. The ONE exception: raw infected-patch occupancy IoU trends ~25-35% below BOTH same-backend baselines (0.165 vs CPM 0.249 / vertex 0.212) — flagged as a candidate weak substrate signal to test at larger scale / more vertex seeds, not attributed to seed noise without evidence. Dose-response direction is strict on both backends across seeds. Initial-state fidelity is exact on CPM and a clean 1:1 on vertex; the adhesion J<->tension mapping is directional. The earlier "fate agrees, morphology diverges" reading was an artifact of comparing a single seed-pair to zero. This is preliminary (reduced scale): the headline N=400 numbers use 3 CPM x 3 vertex seeds (9 cross pairs), and the vertex side is near-degenerate across seeds at this scale (the slow epidemic gives ~identical vertex I-counts; vertex-vs-vertex sd 0.006), so more vertex seeds barely move the result; the lighter CI test uses CPM {0,1,2} vs vertex seed 0. A substrate effect could emerge at larger scale, where the vertex seeds would no longer be degenerate. Known limits: the recruitment latent-pool approximation (T20-RECRUIT), the reduced scale, the producer-less ODE inputs V/L/C/F (Task 21), and the directional adhesion calibration.
decisions_needed: Raw infected-patch occupancy IoU trends ~25-35% below both same-backend baselines (cross 0.165 vs CPM 0.249 / vertex 0.212) — a CANDIDATE weak substrate signal. Test it at a LARGER scale (where the vertex side is no longer near-degenerate across seeds) before calling it signal or noise.
ODE inputs V/L/C/F have no producer (Task 21) — the immune arm is barely exercised at this scale; land the producers to drive recruitment.
Immune recruitment is a latent-pool approximation (T20-RECRUIT) — confirm this is the intended mechanism or replace with topology insertion.
Sego acceptance bands are the CPM stochastic envelope, not digitized Sego 2022 figures — digitize the paper curves for a literature band.
The J<->tension calibration is directional, not pinned — decide whether a sharper calibration (larger sheet) is worth it.

studies.name: adhesion-calibration
studies.question: Can the neutral adhesion be lowered so a mechanics-only sheet has comparable cell-shape statistics on both substrates, and is the J<->tension mapping sharply identified?

findings.statement: The neutral-adhesion -> (CPM J, vertex tension) mapping is directional (monotone) but not sharply identified: vertex cell-shape statistics barely move with tension scale over 0.5..8.

evidence.observed: CPM mean 23.6 / CV 0.098; vertex mean 34.9 / CV 0.064; CV spread < 0.01 across scale

findings.explanation: J and Lambda differ in units/geometry; vertex area is set by area-elasticity + Voronoi, not tension.
findings.next_action: keep tension_scale = 1.0; a larger sheet could sharpen the estimate

studies.claim: A mechanics-only neutral sheet, compiled from one blueprint onto both backends, reaches COMPARABLE cell-shape statistics on the CPM and vertex substrates. The neutral adhesion strength lowers DIRECTLY to the CPM contact energy J and MONOTONICALLY to the vertex line tension; the J<->tension mapping is directional (same sign), not a sharply pinned constant at this scale.

derived.insight: The neutral-adhesion -> (CPM J, vertex tension) mapping is directional (monotone) but not sharply identified: vertex cell-shape statistics barely move with tension scale over 0.5..8.

studies.name: initial-state-fidelity
studies.question: Do both substrates faithfully reproduce the blueprint's initial centroids, sizes and types, and how clean is the vertex 1:1 identity?

findings.statement: The blueprint's t0 state materializes faithfully on both backends (CPM exact; vertex clean 1:1 with a 1.2 um sub-cell residual), so the cross-paradigm comparison begins from a shared initial condition.

evidence.observed: 48/48 type match; CPM RMS 0.000 um; vertex RMS 1.21 um, fraction_clean 1.0, 0 unmapped

findings.explanation: CPM seeds cells 1:1; vertex nearest-centroid assignment over interior faces is uncontested at this spacing.
findings.next_action: none -- fidelity is established; consumed by flu-lung-crossparadigm

studies.claim: Both backends reproduce the blueprint's t=0 state -- every cell's centroid, size and type -- when the one backend-neutral blueprint is compiled onto each. The CPM side is EXACT (centroid residual 0); the vertex side is within a sub-cell residual (RMS ~1.2 um) and achieves a clean 1:1 identity for every cell (fraction_clean 1.0).

derived.insight: The blueprint's t0 state materializes faithfully on both backends (CPM exact; vertex clean 1:1 with a 1.2 um sub-cell residual), so the cross-paradigm comparison begins from a shared initial condition.

studies.name: flu-lung-crossparadigm
studies.question: Does one backend-neutral blueprint reproduce the Sego 2022 influenza model on two different mechanical substrates, and -- judged against same-backend seed noise -- do the substrates diverge?

findings.statement: On cell fate and infected-patch LOCATION the cross-backend difference falls inside the same-backend seed spread (cross fate 0.942 vs CPM 0.934 / vertex 0.943; centroid 6.1 vs 5.4 um; vertex 100% inside the CPM envelope), so at this scale and seed count we FAIL TO REJECT a substrate difference -- a null result, not proof of equality.

evidence.observed: cross 0.942 (0.890-1.000) vs same-backend CPM 0.934 / vertex 0.943; vertex in-band 1.0; N=150 cross == same == 0.987

expected.range: cross within the same-backend seed spread (null control)

findings.explanation: Fate is computed by the shared field/rules/ODE; the substrate enters only via centroid field-sampling + contact-surface, whose effect is not separable from seed noise at this scale/seed count.
findings.next_action: drive the ODE V/L/C/F producers (Task 21) and re-test at larger scale / more vertex seeds, where a substrate effect could become detectable

findings.statement: Raw infected-patch occupancy IoU is the ONE metric trending below BOTH same-backend baselines (cross 0.165 vs CPM 0.249 / vertex 0.212, ~25-35% lower). It is NOT a representation artifact (final mean areas match: CPM 24.67 vs vertex 24.51), so it is flagged as a CANDIDATE weak substrate signal -- not attributed to seed noise, which is untested -- to be checked at larger scale / more seeds.

evidence.observed: final area ratio 0.99; IoU_I cross 0.165 vs same-backend CPM 0.249 / vertex 0.212; centroid 6.1 vs 5.4 um

findings.explanation: Both baselines are low (single-patch scatter), but the cross term sits below both; the vertex Voronoi faces relax to target, ruling out the t0 size confound.
findings.next_action: test the IoU gap with more vertex seeds + a larger/longer run before calling it signal or noise; report IoU only with its same-backend baseline

findings.statement: At faithful Sego rates the per-step infection probability is ~0.004 and the ODE recruitment inflow rounds to ~0 activations, so at reduced scale the epidemic is a slow onset and the latent immune pool is barely activated.

evidence.observed: virus-field integral grows 0 -> ~180 over 400 steps; H/I/D ~30/5/1 (CPM); activations = 0

findings.explanation: Faithful rates + reduced scale + producer-less ODE inputs -> weak drive; not tuned up (anti-goal).
findings.next_action: add the V/L/C/F producers and/or run longer; keep rates faithful

studies.claim: The ONE backend-neutral Sego 2022 influenza blueprint compiles to BOTH the CPM (viva-cpm) and vertex (vivarium-tyssue) substrates and runs the FULL model end-to-end on each. Because the field / rules / systemic-ODE / recruitment mechanism is shared byte-for-byte across the two compiles, we test for a substrate effect against a NULL CONTROL (same-backend seed-to-seed spread). On cell fate and infected-patch LOCATION the cross-backend difference sits inside the same-backend seed spread, so at this scale and seed count we FAIL TO REJECT the null (no detectable substrate effect -- NOT proof of equality). The one exception is raw infected-patch occupancy IoU, which trends ~25-35% below both same-backend baselines -- a candidate weak substrate signal to test at larger scale / more vertex seeds.

derived.insight: On cell fate and infected-patch LOCATION the cross-backend difference falls inside the same-backend seed spread (cross fate 0.942 vs CPM 0.934 / vertex 0.943; centroid 6.1 vs 5.4 um; vertex 100% inside the CPM envelope), so at this scale and seed count we FAIL TO REJECT a substrate difference -- a null result, not proof of equality.

studies.name: dose-response-crossparadigm
studies.question: Do the two substrates agree on the SIGN of the dose response over initial viral load (more load -> more infection), robustly across seeds?

findings.statement: Both substrates show a strictly higher final infection at the highest vs lowest dose, across seeds {0,1} (CPM 1->7 & 1->2, vertex 0->5 & 1->6), agreeing on the direction while intermediate monotonicity is seed-dependent.
findings.explanation: More seed virus raises the shared-field infection probability everywhere; the substrate sets only the noisy magnitude.
findings.next_action: revisit magnitudes once the ODE V producer lands (Task 21)

studies.claim: Both backends agree on the DIRECTION of the dose response: a HIGHER initial viral load (more initially-infected epithelial cells) ends with STRICTLY more infection than a LOWER load, on every backend and seed tested. This is a directional (lowest-vs-highest) result; intermediate-dose monotonicity is seed-dependent and is NOT claimed.

derived.insight: Both substrates show a strictly higher final infection at the highest vs lowest dose, across seeds {0,1} (CPM 1->7 & 1->2, vertex 0->5 & 1->6), agreeing on the direction while intermediate monotonicity is seed-dependent.
